question: Where should uploaded pictures be kept and served from?

choices.label: No picture or file uploads — text-only app
choices.hint: The app does not handle or store file uploads.

choices.label: This machine — no account needed
choices.hint: Files are written under the project and served from it. Fine while building; they do not survive a redeploy.

choices.label: Cloudinary — stores and resizes
choices.hint: One service: the app uploads to it and asks it for whatever size a page needs.

choices.label: Supabase Storage
choices.hint: A bucket with public URLs, and the same project can hold your database. Good if you already use Supabase.

fields.label: Service role key
fields.hint: The same page, under 'service_role'. Server only — it bypasses row-level security, so it must never reach the browser.

fields.label: Bucket name
fields.hint: Storage → Buckets. Create it first; the app will not.

choices.label: ImageBoss — resizes from your own bucket
choices.hint: ImageBoss holds no files. The app uploads to your S3-compatible bucket and ImageBoss reads from it and resizes on the way out, so both halves are needed.

fields.label: Source name
fields.hint: The source you made at imageboss.me — it is the first part of the URL: img.imageboss.me/<source>/…

fields.label: Base path
fields.hint: The path inside the bucket the source points at. Leave as / for the whole bucket.

fields.label: Bucket name
fields.hint: The bucket the app uploads into — the same one you gave ImageBoss.

fields.label: Bucket access key
fields.hint: From your S3, R2, Spaces or Wasabi console — not from ImageBoss.

fields.label: Bucket endpoint
fields.hint: The S3-compatible endpoint for your provider and region.
